result.title: Trust Hinders Bidirectional Human-AI Alignment
result.comment: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026). Workshop: Dynamic Alignment in Human-AI Coupled System (BiAlign Workshop)
result.summary: Trust calibration remains the dominant framing of AI-assisted decision making: the goal is to close the gap between perceived and actual trustworthiness of AI systems so that users exhibit appropriate reliance on them. We argue that this approach, while useful for decision problems that are well-defined and clearly scoped, overly restricts what it means to make a decision with AI support. To overcome this limitation, we develop three dimensions of AI-assisted decision making. First, trusting AI is only one of several possible strategies for managing uncertainty. Second, trust calibration is often misapplied when AI models "large-world" decision problems, i.e., ill-defined situations where goals and states are only partially known or unknowable. Third, in such settings human-AI alignment requires addressing higher-order decision processes. We conclude by reflecting on the implications of our observations on the design of process-oriented human-AI coupled systems that jointly identify and negotiate uncertainty throughout the decision-making task.

AI.brief_summary: 一篇立场论文，主张以「信任校准」主导 AI 辅助决策的框架过于狭窄，转而提出三个维度：信任只是应对不确定性的策略之一、「大世界」问题中信任校准常被误用、此类情境需处理高阶决策过程，并据此讨论面向过程的人机耦合系统设计。
AI.relevance_reason: 其关于不确定性可有多重管理策略、以及在任务过程中动态识别与协商不确定性的讨论，或可类比启发 LVR 中「何时依赖内部 latent 内容、何时追问视觉证据」的策略与停止决策问题；但对象是人的信任而非模型内部状态，属远领域概念线索，需核查。
